_about: Raid writing (Fable, F4). Built by tools/raids_text.py: edit there, not here. The engine reads: boss intro, rooms (three drawn at random from the boss's six; room_pool is the fallback), boss lines, and reactions by hero id (default is the fallback). A room choice rolls one team stat (attack, defense, health, speed, luck). {name} is the hero who reacts, {boss} the boss. The narrator is neutral: no swearing, whatever Smudge's voice setting. Rooms must make sense in any order.

room_pool.text: A door, older than anyone in the team, and locked from the other side. Something behind it is breathing.

choices.label: Kick it in
choices.ok: The door gives on the second kick. The breathing stops.
choices.bad: The door holds. Somebody's ankle does not.

choices.label: Try the handle
choices.ok: It was never locked. Nobody mentions it.
choices.bad: The handle comes off in a hand. The breathing gets closer.

room_pool.text: Half the floor is gone. The other half is thinking about it.

choices.label: Run across
choices.ok: Three pairs of feet, three clean landings.
choices.bad: Somebody finds out where the floor went.

choices.label: Edge along the wall
choices.ok: Slow, careful, and nobody falls.
choices.bad: The wall was the part holding the floor up.

room_pool.text: Two guards, both asleep, both enormous, both lying across the only way through.

choices.label: Tiptoe over them
choices.ok: Not a twitch. The team is through.
choices.bad: One of them wakes up mid-step and is not pleased about it.

choices.label: Wake them up properly
choices.ok: They do not stay awake for long.
choices.bad: They were only pretending to be asleep.

choices.label: Go round the long way
choices.ok: Longer, quieter, fine.
choices.bad: The long way has its own guards.

room_pool.text: The corridor is very clean, very quiet, and full of small holes in the walls.

choices.label: Shields up and walk
choices.ok: Darts bounce off. The team walks out tutting.
choices.bad: Darts do not bounce off everything.

choices.label: Sprint
choices.ok: The darts arrive just after everybody has left.
choices.bad: Some of the darts are faster than some of the team.

room_pool.text: A strongbox, half buried, with a note on it that says DO NOT.

choices.label: Open it
choices.ok: Inside: something useful, and a second note that says FINE.
choices.bad: Inside: a spring, a glove, and a very fast punch.

choices.label: Leave it and push on
choices.ok: The team saves its strength for what is ahead.
choices.bad: Pushing on means walking through the thing that guards the box.

room_pool.text: The weather turns, all at once, as if someone flipped it.

choices.label: Push through it
choices.ok: Soaked, cold, still standing.
choices.bad: The cold gets into everybody's bones.

choices.label: Find shelter
choices.ok: A dry hollow, right where it needed to be.
choices.bad: The shelter is occupied.

tiber.intro: The water off the Roman dock goes very still. Then a long shape moves under it, and keeps moving, and is still the same shape a full minute later. The fishermen of Ostia call it the Tiber Thing, because nobody has seen enough of it to call it anything else.

rooms.text: The fishermen have left their nets, their lunch and one sandal on the quay. None of them is coming back for any of it.

choices.label: Follow the wet footprints
choices.ok: The prints lead the long way round, past the stretch of river that is watching.
choices.bad: The prints stop at the water's edge. So, briefly, does somebody on the team.

choices.label: Eat the lunch
choices.ok: Bread, olives, and a fisherman's sketch of where not to stand. A useful meal.
choices.bad: The fish sauce has been in the sun since Tuesday.

rooms.text: A grain barge drifts sideways across the channel with nobody at the oar. Something bumps it from below, twice, politely, like a knock.

choices.label: Pole it aside
choices.ok: The barge swings clear. The knocking moves off downstream, sounding put out.
choices.bad: The pole comes back shorter, and wet at the wrong end.

choices.label: Climb across while it knocks
choices.ok: Slow hands, steady feet. The barge rocks and nobody goes in.
choices.bad: The third knock is not polite.

rooms.text: A customs officer blocks the pier. He has not noticed the monster. He has noticed that the team has no paperwork.

choices.label: Hand him any scroll
choices.ok: He stamps a laundry list and waves the team through.
choices.bad: It is his own laundry list. He would like to know how the team came by it.

choices.label: Walk briskly and look official
choices.ok: Nobody in Rome stops a group walking that fast.
choices.bad: He blows a whistle. Ostia has more customs officers than anyone guessed.

choices.label: Move him
choices.ok: He is set down gently on a pile of nets, still quoting regulations.
choices.bad: He is heavier than he looks, and he knows the law.

rooms.text: Somebody has left an offering bowl at a small statue of Neptune. The bowl is full. The statue appears to be looking at the team.

choices.label: Leave a coin
choices.ok: The river goes a shade calmer. Probably a coincidence.
choices.bad: The coin bounces out. Neptune has standards.

choices.label: Walk past with heads high
choices.ok: A wave breaks over the pier and finds nobody willing to fall over.
choices.bad: A wave breaks over the pier at chest height, exactly on time.

rooms.text: The far end of the pier is green with weed and missing every third plank. Under the gaps, the water is not moving the way water moves.

choices.label: Hop the gaps
choices.ok: Three hops each, no hesitation. Whatever was waiting has to keep waiting.
choices.bad: The fourth plank was also missing. It had only looked present.

choices.label: Go plank by plank, roped together
choices.ok: Slow and dull and entirely safe.
choices.bad: When one goes through, the rope makes sure everybody joins in.

rooms.text: A stack of amphorae, taller than the team, sways in the river wind. Each one is labelled GARUM. The smell says so too.

choices.label: Push the stack into the river
choices.ok: Forty jars of fish sauce hit the water. Something below gets a faceful and rethinks its evening.
choices.bad: The stack falls the other way. Everyone will smell of this for a week.

choices.label: Edge underneath it
choices.ok: The stack leans, considers, and stays up.
choices.bad: One jar comes down. It is enough.

lines.open: {boss} comes up out of the Tiber, and keeps coming up, with most of the river still running off it.
hit: {boss} lashes out with the end that is mostly teeth.
A wall of river water hits the team, with {boss} somewhere inside it.
{boss} drags somebody under for a moment, then seems to think better of the taste.
A coil the width of a barrel sweeps the pier clean.
lines.low: {boss} is slowing down. More of it is under the water than above it now.
lines.win: {boss} sinks back into the river, length after length, and the water closes over it. For now it stays there.
lines.lose: The team is washed back up the dock, coughing out the Tiber. The long shape goes back to circling.

tony.intro: Behind the speakeasy, in the room with the safe, four gentlemen in good suits are reading four newspapers. Big Tony is not here. Big Tony does not need to be here. That is what the boys are for.

rooms.text: A slot opens in the door. Two eyes look out. A voice asks for the password, and adds that it changed this morning.

choices.label: Guess
choices.ok: 'Swordfish.' The door opens. It is always swordfish.
choices.bad: The slot closes. A larger door opens round the side, and not to be friendly.

choices.label: Knock harder
choices.ok: The door comes off its hinges. The eyes turn out to belong to quite a small man.
choices.bad: The door is steel. The knuckles are not.

rooms.text: The band stops playing when the team walks in. All eight of them. The trumpet player sets his case on the table and opens it slowly.

choices.label: Start dancing
choices.ok: The team hits the floor in step and the band, out of habit, picks the tune back up.
choices.bad: Nobody on the team can dance. It is now a matter of public record.

choices.label: Stand firm and stare
choices.ok: The case contains a trumpet. Everybody breathes out.
choices.bad: The case does not contain a trumpet.

rooms.text: The only way to the back room is through a card game. The players have been at it since Thursday, and a seat has just come free because of how the last player left.

choices.label: Sit in for one hand
choices.ok: Four aces. Nobody is more surprised than the team.
choices.bad: Five aces, one of them the team's. The table does the arithmetic.

choices.label: Walk through and take the shoving
choices.ok: Elbows, chairs, one thrown ashtray. The team arrives on the far side upright.
choices.bad: The players put down their cards to do it properly.

rooms.text: The kitchen is a shortcut. The cook has a cleaver, a temper, and forty pots of something that is, for legal purposes, soup.

choices.label: Run it
choices.ok: In one door and out the other before the cleaver leaves the block.
choices.bad: The floor is as greasy as the soup.

choices.label: Go through behind pot lids
choices.ok: Three clangs, no injuries, and a lid each to keep.
choices.bad: He throws the pots as well.

rooms.text: A small man with a ledger sits outside the back room. He looks the team over and writes down a number. It is not a big number.

choices.label: Change his mind
choices.ok: He crosses the number out and writes a larger one. Respectfully.
choices.bad: He rings a little bell. The number was how many men it would take.

choices.label: Ask what he wrote
choices.ok: He turns the ledger round. It is the odds. He has money on the team.
choices.bad: It is what the team's clothes would fetch. He was being generous.

rooms.text: The cellar stairs are dark, steep, and lined with crates stamped OLIVE OIL. The crates clink.

choices.label: Go down one step at a time
choices.ok: Every step tested, every crate left alone. Quiet as a church.
choices.bad: The ninth step is not attached to anything.

choices.label: Slide down the rail
choices.ok: Fast, silent, and nobody at the bottom has time to look up.
choices.bad: The rail ends before the stairs do.

lines.open: {boss} fold their newspapers, all four at once, and stand up in order of size.
hit: One of {boss} swings a chair with real feeling.
{boss} explain, with their fists, how they feel about the safe.
A gentleman in a good suit throws a very good punch.
{boss} take turns. They are organised about it.
lines.low: Two of {boss} are looking at the door. A third is looking at the window.
lines.win: {boss} leave by the window, one at a time, in order of size. The last one comes back for his hat.
lines.lose: {boss} put the team out in the alley, dust off their hands, and go back to their newspapers.

vanguard.intro: Across the wheat, a line of emus, evenly spaced, perfectly still. They beat the Australian army in 1932 and have been waiting ever since for somebody to send another one. The bird at the centre of the line has a medal. Nobody knows who gave it to him.

rooms.text: The army's old trench runs toward the birds. In it: spent cartridges, a kettle, and a note that says only WE TRIED.

choices.label: Crawl along the trench
choices.ok: Heads down the whole way. The line of birds never turns.
choices.bad: The trench ends early. The army left in a hurry and did not finish it.

choices.label: Go over the top at a sprint
choices.ok: Up, across and down again before a single neck swivels.
choices.bad: It is the plan the army used.

rooms.text: One emu stands on a rise, facing the team. It blinks once. Somewhere behind it, a great many feet shift.

choices.label: Rush it before it reports
choices.ok: It gets three steps. The report is never filed.
choices.bad: It was never the scout. It was the bait.

choices.label: Stand very still too
choices.ok: After a long minute the emu decides the team is a shrub.
choices.bad: After a long minute the emu decides the team is lunch.

rooms.text: Head-high wheat in every direction. Something is moving through it in a line, and the line is turning.

choices.label: Cut a path straight through
choices.ok: A straight road through the crop, and whatever was circling loses the scent.
choices.bad: The noise of cutting tells the whole field exactly where to come.

choices.label: Pick a direction and commit
choices.ok: The team walks out of the wheat on the right side of it, by no skill at all.
choices.bad: The team walks out of the wheat where it walked in. There are tracks over its tracks.

rooms.text: An abandoned Lewis gun sits on its tripod, pointed at the horizon. There is a beak mark on the barrel.

choices.label: Get it working
choices.ok: It fires for nine glorious seconds. The birds remember that sound, and not fondly.
choices.bad: It jams at once. The army could have told them that.

choices.label: Take the armour plate off it
choices.ok: A decent shield, lightly pecked.
choices.bad: It is bolted on. The clanging carries for miles.

rooms.text: The rabbit-proof fence runs to both horizons. It was never meant to be emu-proof, as the large emu-shaped hole in it explains.

choices.label: Climb it
choices.ok: Wire, splinters, and over. Nothing that will not heal.
choices.bad: The top strand is barbed. So is the second, and the third.

choices.label: Go through the hole before its owner comes back
choices.ok: Through and gone. The hole stays empty.
choices.bad: Its owner had not gone far.

rooms.text: A farmer leans on a gatepost and watches the team pass. 'After the birds, are you,' he says. It is not a question. He has seen this before.

choices.label: Ask his advice
choices.ok: 'Don't run in a straight line.' It is the best advice anyone has had all year.
choices.bad: 'Go home.' He means it kindly, and he will not say more.

choices.label: Accept a cup of tea
choices.ok: The tea could hold a spoon upright. Everyone feels braver.
choices.bad: The tea has been in the pot since 1929.

lines.open: {boss} charge all at once, in silence, faster than anything with those legs should move.
hit: {boss} run straight through the team and wheel round for another pass.
One emu kicks with the force of a small car.
{boss} scatter, re-form, and come back in from the side.
A beak finds a gap in somebody's guard. Then several more beaks find it.
lines.low: {boss} are thinning out. The one with the medal has stopped to think.
lines.win: {boss} withdraw in good order, without looking back. They will remember this, and they have long memories.
lines.lose: The team retreats across the wheat. The emus do not give chase. They have never needed to.

gary.intro: Between the flags at Bondi, a fin, going round in slow, confident circles. The lifeguards know him. The council knows him. He is Gary, he is a great white, and he has decided that the safe swimming area is his.

rooms.text: The sign says BEACH CLOSED. Under it, a second sign says WE MEAN IT. Under that, a third, handwritten: GARY.

choices.label: Go round by the rocks
choices.ok: Careful feet on wet stone. The long way, and the dry way.
choices.bad: The rocks are covered in oysters. Oysters are sharp all over.

choices.label: Vault the barrier
choices.ok: Over in one and down the sand before anyone can blow a whistle.
choices.bad: The barrier was the dry part. The team lands in the wet part.

rooms.text: A rip current runs out through the middle of the bay, flat and fast and harmless-looking.

choices.label: Swim straight across it
choices.ok: Hard going, lungs burning, and out the other side.
choices.bad: The sea wins that one and does not rush it.

choices.label: Ride it out and cut sideways
choices.ok: Out past the break and round the back, the way the lifeguards teach it.
choices.bad: The rip delivers the team somewhere, at speed. It is not the somewhere they wanted.

rooms.text: Forty tourists stand at the waterline filming the fin. None of them will move, in case they miss something.

choices.label: Clear the beach
choices.ok: Forty people discover they can run in thongs after all.
choices.bad: Forty people film the team instead, and do not get out of the way.

choices.label: Shout 'free sunscreen'
choices.ok: The beach empties toward the kiosk. Nobody has to be eaten today.
choices.bad: They already have sunscreen. They would like to know what else is free.

rooms.text: A flock of seagulls has claimed the path to the rock pool. Somebody on the team is holding chips.

choices.label: Run for it
choices.ok: Gone before the first gull has finished shouting about it.
choices.bad: Nothing on this beach outruns a seagull.

choices.label: Hand over the chips
choices.ok: A fair toll. The gulls stand aside, almost respectfully.
choices.bad: The gulls take the chips and then, on principle, a hat.

rooms.text: The tide has left a line of bluebottles across the sand, blue and shiny and thin as a mistake.

choices.label: Pick a way through
choices.ok: Eyes down, one careful step at a time. Not a single sting.
choices.bad: The one nobody saw is always the one.

choices.label: Walk straight over them
choices.ok: Thick hide and thicker boots. Nothing gets through.
choices.bad: How bad could it be? Quite bad. The answer was quite bad.

rooms.text: The lifeguard tower is empty. The radio is still on. A voice keeps asking whether anyone has eyes on Gary.

choices.label: Take the binoculars
choices.ok: From up here the pattern is plain: he always turns left.
choices.bad: The binoculars show Gary very clearly. He is looking back.

choices.label: Take the rescue board
choices.ok: Eight feet of fibreglass. As clubs go, it has reach.
choices.bad: It snaps on the first wave. Half a board each.

lines.open: {boss} comes up out of the surf, mouth first.
hit: {boss} takes a bite out of the afternoon.
{boss} thrashes, and half the rock pool goes with him.
{boss} circles once and comes back in from below.
A tail the size of a door catches somebody mid-stride.
lines.low: {boss} is swimming crooked. He keeps glancing at the open sea.
lines.win: {boss} turns out past the flags and keeps going, as if leaving had been his idea.
lines.lose: The lifeguards haul the team up the sand and put the BEACH CLOSED sign back. Gary resumes his circles.

nephew.intro: The Doge's vault has one guard who matters: the Doge's nephew. He has a sword, eleven years of the best lessons in Venice, and a face nobody has ever said no to. He is not good at guarding. He is very good at the other thing.

rooms.text: The only way in is by water. The gondolier names a price, looks at the team again, and doubles it.

choices.label: Haggle
choices.ok: He is so pleased to be argued with properly that he throws in a song.
choices.bad: He doubles it again, and the song is extra.

choices.label: Take the gondola while he talks
choices.ok: The team is three bridges away before he reaches the end of the sentence.
choices.bad: It is harder to steer than he makes it look. The canal is cold.

rooms.text: The palace is holding a masked ball. Every guest has a mask. The team has, between them, one napkin.

choices.label: Walk in as if invited
choices.ok: A footman bows. Somebody is handed a drink. Venice assumes the best of the well dressed.
choices.bad: The napkin fools nobody, and the footmen are larger up close.

choices.label: Cross the floor during the dance
choices.ok: In at one door, out at the other, and never out of step.
choices.bad: The dance changes partners. The team is separated, twirled, and returned bruised.

rooms.text: A corridor of portraits: six hundred years of Doges, every one painted looking disappointed. The floorboards beneath them creak in sequence.

choices.label: Move between the creaks
choices.ok: Step, wait, step. Not a sound.
choices.bad: The floor keeps time better than the team does.

choices.label: Walk normally and own it
choices.ok: Nobody questions people who walk as if they are late for a meeting.
choices.bad: A guard questions people who walk as if they are late for a meeting.

rooms.text: The vault door has a lock made by a genius: forty tumblers, three false keyholes, and a small brass plate that says GOOD LUCK in Latin.

choices.label: Pick it
choices.ok: The fortieth tumbler drops. The genius, wherever he is, feels a chill.
choices.bad: The second keyhole was false. It was also sharp.

choices.label: Take the hinges off instead
choices.ok: The genius did not make the hinges. A nobody made the hinges.
choices.bad: The genius also made the hinges.

rooms.text: The guard is asleep on a chair with the keys on his belt. He was hired by the nephew. It shows.

choices.label: Lift the keys
choices.ok: He snores through it and smiles at something in a dream.
choices.bad: He sleeps with one hand on the keys. The other hand holds a bell.

choices.label: Leave him and try the door
choices.ok: The door is open. He was hired by the nephew.
choices.bad: The door is locked, and the handle squeaks.

rooms.text: The nephew's fencing master is in the anteroom, practising against six straw dummies. Five are already in pieces.

choices.label: Hold a guard and edge past
choices.ok: He nods at the footwork and lets it go by. A professional courtesy.
choices.bad: He corrects the guard. With the point.

choices.label: Offer him a real opponent
choices.ok: He is delighted, then beaten, then delighted again. He bows the team through.
choices.bad: He has waited years for a real opponent. He makes it last.

lines.open: {boss} salutes, very correctly, and attacks before anybody can salute back.
hit: {boss} lunges, perfectly, exactly as he was taught.
{boss} disarms somebody and hands the weapon back, which is worse.
{boss} parries three blows and answers all three.
A flick of the wrist, and somebody has a new buttonhole.
lines.low: {boss} has started checking his hair between strikes. It is no longer perfect, and it is bothering him.
lines.win: {boss} yields, very correctly, and asks only that nobody mention this to his uncle.
lines.lose: {boss} has the team shown out of the vault, politely, by eight guards. He waves.

well.intro: In the witch's clearing there is an old well with a new lid, and the lid is moving. Whatever is under it was put there a long time ago by people who knew what they were doing. Then Smudge came along with a shovel.

rooms.text: The path into the forest forks. One way has a carved sign. The other has a newer sign, in different handwriting, saying that the first sign lies.

choices.label: Pick a sign and trust it
choices.ok: It was the honest one. There is no way to know that, even afterwards.
choices.bad: Both signs lie. The forest has a sense of humour.

choices.label: Ignore both and cut through the trees
choices.ok: Straight through, branches whipping, and out before the forest can rearrange itself.
choices.bad: The trees are closer together than they were a moment ago.

rooms.text: A cottage made of gingerbread stands by the path, with smoke in the chimney and a welcome mat. The mat is also gingerbread. The whole thing is extremely obvious.

choices.label: Eat some anyway
choices.ok: It is very good gingerbread. Whatever comes next, the team meets it fed.
choices.bad: It is very old gingerbread.

choices.label: Walk past, touching nothing
choices.ok: The door opens a crack as the team passes, and closes again, disappointed.
choices.bad: The path past the cottage is gingerbread too. It gives way.

rooms.text: Every branch above the path has a raven on it. None of them makes a sound. All of them face the same way: toward the team.

choices.label: Greet them politely
choices.ok: One raven nods. The rest look away. Manners still count for something out here.
choices.bad: The ravens confer, briefly, and reach a decision.

choices.label: Scatter them
choices.ok: A storm of black wings, and then an empty sky.
choices.bad: They scatter, and then they come back, and now it is personal.

rooms.text: The ground here has been dug and filled in many times, by many different shovels. The newest hole is still open, and it is the right size for the whole team.

choices.label: Jump it
choices.ok: Over, one after another, without looking down.
choices.bad: It is wider at the far side than it was at the near side.

choices.label: Fill it in
choices.ok: Whatever was on its way up finds the way blocked, and goes back down to think.
choices.bad: Something on the other side of the dirt is digging faster.

rooms.text: The roots across the path were not across the path a moment ago.

choices.label: Chop through them
choices.ok: They part, twitching, and do not grow back while anyone is looking.
choices.bad: They grow back while everyone is looking.

choices.label: Step through before they close
choices.ok: Quick feet. The roots close on empty air.
choices.bad: The roots close on an ankle.

rooms.text: A lantern hangs from a branch, burning green, with nobody holding it. It swings toward the team like a head turning.

choices.label: Follow it
choices.ok: It leads the long way round, past everything with teeth, and goes out at the clearing's edge like a job done.
choices.bad: It leads the team in a circle and goes out laughing.

choices.label: Put it out
choices.ok: Dark, but an honest dark.
choices.bad: It does not go out. It goes somewhere else, and takes the light with it.

lines.open: {boss} climbs out of the well. It takes a long time. There is a great deal of it.
hit: {boss} reaches out of the dark and pulls.
Something in the well whispers, and everyone hears their own name.
{boss} lashes the clearing with roots that were not there a moment ago.
The ground under the team opens, a little, experimentally.
lines.low: {boss} is sagging back toward the well, as if the daylight is heavy.
lines.win: {boss} goes back down the well. The lid goes back on. Somebody sits on it until the knocking stops.
lines.lose: The team runs from the clearing and does not look back, which is the only wise thing anyone has done all day.

antlers.intro: Far out on the fjord there is a hole in the ice that nobody cut. Something with antlers lives under it, older than the village, older than the name of the fjord. The fishermen leave it a cod each winter and do not ask what it does with them.

rooms.text: The fjord ice groans underfoot. Toward the middle it changes colour, from white to grey to a dark that is not an ice colour at all.

choices.label: Spread out and go slowly
choices.ok: The ice complains the whole way and holds the whole way.
choices.bad: The ice had been waiting for exactly that much weight.

choices.label: Run the thin part
choices.ok: Light feet, long strides. The cracks open behind the team, not under it.
choices.bad: The cracks are faster.

rooms.text: A fishing hut stands alone on the ice. The fire inside is still lit. The line through the floor is still out, and it is pulling the hut, slowly, toward the middle of the fjord.

choices.label: Haul the line in
choices.ok: A cod the size of a door comes up. Not what they came for, but supper, and proof the line holds.
choices.bad: The line hauls back.

choices.label: Cut the line and warm up
choices.ok: Ten minutes by a fire is worth a great deal up here.
choices.bad: The hut, cut loose, was the only thing holding that patch of ice in place.

rooms.text: The snow comes in sideways, all at once, and takes the far shore with it.

choices.label: Walk into it
choices.ok: Heads down, one foot and then the other. The storm gives up first.
choices.bad: The cold gets into the bones and takes a seat.

choices.label: Wait it out
choices.ok: It passes in minutes, as if it had somewhere else to be.
choices.bad: It does not pass. It settles in and gets comfortable.

rooms.text: A longship is frozen into the ice at an angle, oars still out. Someone carved a warning on the prow, and under it, in a later hand, a tally of the people who ignored it.

choices.label: Shelter along the hull
choices.ok: Out of the wind for the length of a ship. A small mercy, gratefully taken.
choices.bad: The hull shifts. It has been waiting a hundred years to finish sinking.

choices.label: Break off the oars for spears
choices.ok: Good ash, seasoned by a century of frost. They will do.
choices.bad: The oars are frozen in. The ice lets go of the team's footing first.

rooms.text: A colony of seals lies across the only solid ice. They are large, numerous, and have the look of creatures that have never once been made to move.

choices.label: Dart between them
choices.ok: Through the gaps and away before a single head lifts.
choices.bad: A seal rolls over at the wrong moment. It is like being hit by a wet sofa.

choices.label: Wade through and take the slaps
choices.ok: Flippers from every side, and the team keeps walking.
choices.bad: There are more seals than there is team.

rooms.text: Under the clear ice, something keeps pace with the team. When they stop, it stops. Its shadow has too many points.

choices.label: Outrun it to the hole
choices.ok: It loses interest, or pretends to.
choices.bad: It knew where the team was going. It gets there first.

choices.label: Stand still until it leaves
choices.ok: A long minute. Then the shadow sinks, and the ice is only ice again.
choices.bad: It does not leave. It taps once, from below, to see what the ice will take.

lines.open: {boss} breaks the ice from below, antlers first, and the whole fjord rings like a bell.
hit: {boss} swings its antlers in a wide, freezing arc.
The ice cracks under the team, and {boss} is waiting underneath.
{boss} breathes out, and the cold arrives like a blow.
A point of antler the length of an oar comes up through the ice between somebody's feet.
lines.low: {boss} is breathing hard. The ice around it has gone soft and grey.
lines.win: {boss} sinks back under the ice without a sound, and the hole freezes over behind it, smooth as glass.
lines.lose: The team is dragged off the fjord half frozen. Behind them the hole is still open, and something in it is still looking up.

brenda.intro: Brenda from Facilities is back from leave. In three weeks away she has not forgotten one thing about this office, and in ten minutes back she has seen the state of the supply closet. She has the only key. She is standing in the doorway. She would like a word.

rooms.text: Reception wants every visitor signed in. The sheet asks for name, company, time in and purpose of visit. The pen is on a chain. The chain is too short.

choices.label: Write 'meeting'
choices.ok: Nobody in this building has ever questioned a meeting.
choices.bad: The receptionist asks which meeting. The pause lasts most of a quarter.

choices.label: Walk past on a phone call
choices.ok: 'No, I hear you, I hear you.' The team is through the barrier before the nod is finished.
choices.bad: The barrier needs a pass. It closes at hip height.

rooms.text: The printer in the corridor is jammed, flashing, and blocking the way. A sign taped to it reads DO NOT TOUCH. BRENDA KNOWS.

choices.label: Unjam it by force
choices.ok: One sheet comes out. Then two hundred more. The way is clear and the team is, briefly, popular.
choices.bad: PC LOAD LETTER. The printer bites.

choices.label: Squeeze past without touching it
choices.ok: Breath held, elbows in. The printer flashes on, none the wiser.
choices.bad: An elbow brushes the paper tray. Somewhere, a log is updated.

rooms.text: The open-plan floor. Sixty desks. Anyone who makes eye contact will be asked whether they have five minutes.

choices.label: Cross it fast
choices.ok: Eyes front, pace brisk. Sixty heads stay down.
choices.bad: 'Quick one while you're passing.' It is not a quick one.

choices.label: Carry a laptop and look worried
choices.ok: The universal pass. Nobody stops a person carrying a laptop and looking worried.
choices.bad: Somebody needs that exact laptop.

rooms.text: The kitchen. In the fridge is a yoghurt with a label on it. The label says BRENDA. It went out of date while she was away.

choices.label: Eat it and remove the evidence
choices.ok: A brave act and a terrible yoghurt. No evidence remains.
choices.bad: It fights back, from the inside.

choices.label: Change the date on the label
choices.ok: A steady hand and the right pen. It will buy a day.
choices.bad: The pen is permanent. The handwriting is not hers. She will know.

rooms.text: A meeting has spilled out into the corridor. It was booked for thirty minutes. That was this morning.

choices.label: Sit through it
choices.ok: Forty minutes of slides. The team comes out older, unharmed, and aligned on next steps.
choices.bad: There are action items. The team now owns three of them.

choices.label: Say 'hard stop' and keep walking
choices.ok: The two words nobody can argue with. The meeting parts like a sea.
choices.bad: 'Before you go.' Nobody has ever escaped a 'before you go'.

rooms.text: The key cupboard is where it has always been, behind the fire warden's desk. The fire warden is at the desk. He takes the role seriously.

choices.label: Ask to borrow the closet key
choices.ok: He hands over a form. It is one page long. A miracle.
choices.bad: He hands over a form. The form has a form.

choices.label: Wait for his tea break
choices.ok: Half past ten exactly. He is a man of routine. The cupboard is unguarded for four minutes.
choices.bad: Today he takes his tea at the desk.

lines.open: {boss} rolls up her sleeves and closes the closet door behind her. The lock clicks.
hit: {boss} throws a stapler with frightening accuracy.
{boss} asks who used the last of the printer paper, and it lands like a blow.
{boss} reorganises somebody, by force.
{boss} produces the sign-out sheet. Nobody on the team has ever signed it. She reads the blanks aloud.
lines.low: {boss} has looked at the clock twice. It is nearly five.
lines.win: {boss} signs herself out for the day, to the minute, and leaves the closet to the team. She will be back at nine.
lines.lose: {boss} sends the team to HR. It is the worst thing that has ever happened to any of them.
